name: Gravity canals, upper Zaña valley, northern Peru
summary: Excavated, partly stone-lined gravity canals in northern Peru are early evidence of small-scale irrigation in South America.
description: At Quebrada sin Nombre-1 in the Ñanchoc Valley, partly stone-lined channels run along an upper terrace above the stream. The excavators associate Canals 3 and 2 with the Tierra Blanca phase and infer that the canals supplied fields on the lower bench. Both buried channels are dated by associated charcoal in their fill. A much later surface canal overlies them.

impact.note: Small gravity canals could supply water to plots in a seasonally dry valley within a mixed farming and foraging economy. The superimposed canals show rebuilding in one valley, with episodes of burial between channels. Descent of later coastal Andean irrigation remains an open question.

date.label: c. 4360-3990 BCE
date.basis: Published 2005 calibration of charcoal from the sandy channel fill (Beta-154127).

events.statement: Charcoal from the sandy fill of Canal 3 at Quebrada sin Nombre-1 dates to 6310–5940 cal BP in the 2005 report. The excavators associate the channel with the Tierra Blanca phase.

evidence.supports: Canal 3 is a stone-lined channel sampled for charcoal from its sandy fill. The excavators associate Canals 2 and 3 with Tierra Blanca and publish the 2σ range of 6310–5940 cal BP for Beta-154127.
evidence.locator: pp. 17241–17243, stratigraphic cuts and charcoal sampling, phase association, and Fig. 2 (canal profile and radiocarbon dates)

evidence.supports: The table lists Beta-154127 under Tierra Blanca and gives 6279–5936 cal BP for the same charcoal sample.

events.caveats: Fill charcoal provides an associated age. The date of construction and the period of operation remain unresolved.

date.label: c. 3100-2910 BCE
date.basis: Published 2005 calibration of charcoal from the sandy channel fill (Beta-182966).

events.statement: Charcoal from the sandy fill of Canal 2 at Quebrada sin Nombre-1 dates to 5050–4860 cal BP in the 2005 report. The excavators associate the channel with the Tierra Blanca phase.

evidence.supports: Canal 2 is a stone-lined channel sampled for charcoal from its sandy fill. The excavators associate Canals 2 and 3 with Tierra Blanca and publish the 2σ range of 5050–4860 cal BP for Beta-182966.
evidence.locator: pp. 17241–17243, stratigraphic cuts and charcoal sampling, phase association, and Fig. 2 (canal profile and radiocarbon dates)

evidence.supports: The table lists Beta-182966 under Tierra Blanca and gives 5038–4833 cal BP for the same charcoal sample.

events.caveats: Fill charcoal provides an associated age. The date of construction and the period of operation remain unresolved.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: A possible fourth canal below Canal 3 is dated 6,705 ± 75 radiocarbon years BP (8,040-7,340 cal. BP); the paper treats it as possible only.
Whether the valley-wide and inter-valley canal systems of the Moche and Chimú descend from these canals is not covered by the source read.
The lead's 'possibly c. 4700 BCE' was not found in the paper.
The buried field below the canals remains undated. A dated field horizon or a stratigraphically traced outlet would help establish which canal served it.

evidence.locator: pp. 17243–17244, Fig. 3 and discussion of the lower bench and garden sites
evidence.supports: The lower-bench field is undated. The excavated furrows at CA-09-27 and CA-09-52 are on a separate fan and have earlier contexts.

unresolved.about: Hydraulic and archaeological fit of the lower bench
unresolved.note: The excavators modeled water delivery from different intakes and slopes to the same bench. Tracing an excavated outlet to the field would distinguish the modeled destination from an observed connection.

evidence.locator: pp. 17242–17244 and Fig. 3, hydraulic comparison of Canals 1–3
evidence.supports: A same-field interpretation informed the slope and flow comparison. The lower-bench field is undated.

research.note: Dillehay and colleagues call the Zaña valley canals the earliest known in South America, and contact with Old World irrigators at this date was impossible. Event bounds use the 2005 calibration. Dillehay et al. 2007, Table 1, gives different calibrated ranges for the same assays. Canal 2 lies close to the younger boundary in the 2011 Tierra Blanca chronology.
